Our 40-point projection sits a point under the 41 total, and 66% of total money is on the Under. That fits the slow-tempo read but isn't enough to act on. <details class="rollup-box section-4" id="confidence-defs">
<summary>📖 How the stars work</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Stars show how much evidence lines up behind a bet**, compared with our other bets this week. More stars = a stronger case. They are **not** a win percentage.
- **Where a bet starts:** ★★★½ when our own matchup numbers **and** at least two named experts back it · ★★★ when our matchup numbers back it · ★★½ when at least two named experts picked it · ★★ when the support is only partial.
- **Up half a star** when the experts are lopsided in its favor (at least four of them, two-to-one or better), or when the big-money bettors are on the same side.
- **Down half a star** when more experts picked the other side, when the big money is on the other side, or when an injury or lineup question is still open.
- We do not use a computer model's win percentage here: ours failed its accuracy test, so it is left out.

## 3. Teaser Bets: 6-Point Wong Teasers

<div class="rollup-controls">
  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-3', true)">Expand Section 3</button>

<details class="rollup-box section-main secmain-3" id="section-3-box" open>
<summary>🔁 Section 3: Teaser Bets: 6-Point Wong Teasers</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">



**What a teaser is:** you move the point spread 6 points in your favor on every leg, in exchange for a smaller payout, and every leg must win. The "Wong" version only uses lines where those 6 points cross both **3 and 7**, the two most common NFL winning margins: favorites of −7.5 to −8.5 (teased down to −1.5 / −2.5) and underdogs of +1.5 to +2.5 (teased up to +7.5 / +8.5). Keep teasers to 2 legs.

Each game opens with a written game script, our projected final score and the reasoning behind the card lean, with links to the experts cited and the actionable props for that game. Below that: the betting lines, key context, and every pick grouped by **sides**, **totals** and **player props**.




**What the betting lines are predicting.** Every point spread and total is really a forecast. Put the two together and you get the final score the sportsbook expects; the moneylines give each team's chance of winning. Next to that is **our own projected score** (from the game write-ups in [Section 6](#section-6-box)) and **where the bets and the money are landing**, on both sides of every market.

<details class="rollup-box section-synth" id="board-defs">
<summary>📖 What each column means (plain English)</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Favorite & spread:** the team expected to win and by how many points. "BUF −7" means Buffalo has to win by 8 or more for a Buffalo spread bet to cash.
- **Total points:** the combined score the sportsbook set as its over/under line.
- **Score the lines imply:** the final score the spread and total point to together. Example: total 50.5 and BUF −7 → Buffalo about 28.8, Chargers about 21.8.
- **Our projection:** Platinum Rose's own projected final: the line, adjusted for injuries, matchups, expert opinion and money moves. Not a computer-model output.
- **Win chance:** each moneyline turned into a win probability, with the sportsbook's built-in cut removed so the two sides add up to 100%.
- **Spread / Total (bets / money):** for each side, the share of bets placed and the share of dollars wagered. Example: "O 25/51 · U 75/49" means only 25% of bets are on the Over but they carry 51% of the money.
- **💰 Big-money signal:** a side where the money share beats the bet share by 15+ points — fewer, bigger bets, usually experienced ("sharp") bettors. We record **the exact line when the signal first appears**, so later builds show whether the line has moved toward or away from that side since.

</div>
</details>

<summary>⏰ Sun 06:30 PT — <span class="tl tl-phi" title="Philadelphia Eagles"></span>Philadelphia Eagles @ <span class="tl tl-jax" title="Jacksonville Jaguars"></span>Jacksonville Jaguars — JAX -8 · O/U 41 · Proj PHI 16 – JAX 24</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

<div class="game-narrative" style="border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); background: rgba(0,210,190,0.07); padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 8px; margin: 4px 0 16px 0;">
<div style="font-size: 1.08rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 4px;">🎯 Projected final: JAX 24, PHI 16</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; opacity: 0.85; margin-bottom: 8px;">lines imply JAX 24.5 – PHI 16.5 · projected margin JAX by 8 → covers: push (JAX -8) · total 40 vs 41 → Under</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; margin-bottom: 8px;">📈 <strong>Line movement</strong> (opening line: Action Network open, Sun 10/4 5:00 PM PT → Bookmaker now, 2026-10-11): spread JAX -3.5 → -8 · total 43.5 → 41 · moneyline PHI +155 → +323 · moneyline JAX -182 → -389</div>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">This one is billed as a London game (VSiN lists it as "Eagles +7.5 vs Jaguars (London)"), which takes some of the shine off Jacksonville's home edge. The Jaguars still have the cleaner offense, 0.173 EPA per play against Philadelphia's -0.107 in the FTN tables. Trevor Lawrence leans on Bhayshul Tuten, who has run for 66, 65, 73 and 73 yards in four games and is the shortest anytime-TD price on the board at -110. Lawrence's targets on the MEDIUM secondary matchup are Jakobi Meyers, Brenton Strange and Brian Thomas Jr., while Philadelphia is badly short-handed: Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Hollywood Brown and center Drew Kendall are all Out. That leaves Jalen Hurts throwing to Dallas Goedert (41+ receiving yards at -108), Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon. Their matchup is graded HIGH (severity 6.45) against a Jacksonville secondary that lists Eric Murray as Doubtful. Both teams run about 57 plays a game, so expect a slow, field-goal-heavy middle. Jacksonville wins 24-16. The eight-point margin lands right on the -8, a push at Bookmaker's number.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">The Opus run rates this game as conflicted and passes. All of the tier-eligible evidence comes from VSiN: Matt Youmans, Zachary Cohen and Dave Tuley, all on Philadelphia at +7.5 or +8. That counts as one outlet, and the numbers disagree with it. FTN, the Out list and a provisional model margin of 9.07 all point to Jacksonville. The registry has 7 experts on JAX, among them <a href="#exp-phi-jax-bettingpros">Andrew Erickson</a>, <a href="#exp-phi-jax-bettingpros">BettingPros</a>, <a href="#exp-phi-jax-daniel-jeremiah-bucky-brooks">Daniel Jeremiah & Bucky Brooks</a> and Pro Football Talk, and <a href="#exp-phi-jax-the-favorites">The Favorites</a> and <a href="#exp-phi-jax-even-money">Even Money</a> also back the Jaguars in the side picks. The moneyline is louder: PHI +323 has 28% of bets but 50% of the money, though the price has drifted from +295 to +323, away from Philadelphia. Our 40-point projection sits a point under the 41 total, and 66% of total money is on the Under. That fits the slow-tempo read but isn't enough to act on. The spread already moved from -7.5 to -8 through the hook. The 02:21 PT capture expires before the 06:30 PT kickoff, so every price needs a fresh capture.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">The pocket. Philadelphia is without Kendall at center, already takes sacks on 8.7% of dropbacks and drops to -0.628 EPA per dropback under pressure. The reverse path is Hurts finding Goedert and Wicks against the thinned secondary. That keeps the game inside a touchdown and makes 7 the number that matters.</p>

<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Tyson Bagent starts for Chicago. In his Week 4 start he went 25 of 34 for 268 yards and no touchdowns, and <a href="#exp-chi-gb-bettingpros">BettingPros</a> backs his rushing line Over 10.5. With Kyle Monangai (Out), the Bears' cleanest scoring look is Luther Burden III in the slot. He leads the team with six red-zone targets and is priced around +240/+250 to score. Chicago plays long, at 74.5 plays a game and about 35 minutes of possession, which keeps Green Bay's offense on the sideline. That offense is the weakest unit on the field: -0.089 EPA per play, and -0.481 EPA per dropback under pressure. Chicago pressures on 35.3% of dropbacks, and Green Bay's interior linemen Jacob Monk and Aaron Banks are both Doubtful. Jordan Love still has the HIGH secondary matchup (severity 5.25) against a Chicago defense without Kyler Gordon. He throws to Matthew Golden, Skyy Moore and Tucker Kraft, who is +250 to score. His yardage line is 243+, and BettingPros notes he has never thrown more than 32 passes in six starts against Chicago. Gusts near 42 km/h are a mild drag on throwing and kicking. It plays out as a one-point Bears win, 24-23, which leaves Green Bay covering the +1.5.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">The Opus run passes with a zero margin hypothesis. Chicago's better four-game profile (SRS 12.1 vs -7.4) is offset by the backup QB, Chicago's defensive absences and a +47 point differential built mostly in one 59-37 game. The market has already priced the switch to Bagent. Our projection lands inside the 1.5, which matches the earlier research-only GB +1.5 lean, but a one-point edge on a near coin-flip spread is noise. The only tier-eligible side pick was VSiN's Packers ML at +120. That price is now +103, so the pick no longer exists at its number. The registry splits 10 on GB, including <a href="#exp-chi-gb-action-network">Action Network</a>, <a href="#exp-chi-gb-bettingpros">Andrew Erickson</a>, Brandon Kravitz, <a href="#exp-chi-gb-even-money">Even Money</a> and <a href="#exp-chi-gb-even-money">Ross Tucker</a>, with <a href="#exp-chi-gb-the-favorites">The Favorites</a> and BettingPros also on Green Bay in the side picks. Five are on CHI: <a href="#exp-chi-gb-daniel-jeremiah-bucky-brooks">Daniel Jeremiah & Bucky Brooks</a>, Matt Perrault, Pro Football Talk and <a href="#exp-chi-gb-sharp-or-square">Sharp or Square</a>. BettingPros has the lone Over. Spread bets are 57% CHI but money is only 52%, a 5-point tilt to Green Bay with no big-money signal. The total has climbed from 44.5 to 47, with 74% of bets on the Over. Our 47 matches the line, and the wind is worth half a point to the Under at most. The 04:00 PT capture expires before the 10:00 PT kickoff, so prices must be recaptured.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Caleb Williams is still listed Questionable. If he starts instead of Bagent, Chicago gets repriced upward toward 3, the key number where about 8% of games land, and a one-point game becomes a field-goal-plus Bears win. If Monk and Banks both sit, Chicago's pressure meets an offense that collapses under it, and sacks and turnovers on Love could stretch the margin past a touchdown. The Green Bay path runs the other way. Bagent's interceptions prop is Over 0.5 at -102, so one giveaway is close to a coin flip. With Gordon out, Love hitting Golden and Kraft early turns this into a Packers win by a field goal or more.</p>

<summary>⏰ Sun 10:00 PT — <span class="tl tl-hou" title="Houston Texans"></span>Houston Texans @ <span class="tl tl-ten" title="Tennessee Titans"></span>Tennessee Titans — HOU -7 · O/U 37.5 · Proj HOU 22 – TEN 15</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

<div class="game-narrative" style="border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); background: rgba(0,210,190,0.07); padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 8px; margin: 4px 0 16px 0;">
<div style="font-size: 1.08rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 4px;">🎯 Projected final: HOU 22, TEN 15</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; opacity: 0.85; margin-bottom: 8px;">lines imply HOU 22.2 – TEN 15.2 · projected margin HOU by 7 → covers: push (HOU -7) · total 37 vs 37.5 → Under</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; margin-bottom: 8px;">📈 <strong>Line movement</strong> (opening line: Action Network open, Sun 10/4 5:00 PM PT → Bookmaker now, 2026-10-11): spread HOU -6.5 → -7 · total 39.5 → 37.5 · moneyline HOU -317 → -340 · moneyline TEN +243 → +286</div>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Two 0-4 division rivals, and the loser falls to 0-5. C.J. Stroud is Houston's edge. He has thrown for 274, 353, 167 and 347 yards with no interceptions, and the HIGH secondary matchup (severity 5.85) points him at Nico Collins, Dalton Schultz and Kayshon Boutte against a Tennessee pass defense allowing 0.196 EPA per dropback. Collins is the shortest anytime-TD price at +118, with a receiving line of 77.5. Tennessee hasn't topped 20 points in any game and runs the slowest pace in the matchup at 54 plays per game. Cam Ward throws short (6.5-yard average depth of target) to Wan'Dale Robinson, Elic Ayomanor, Gunnar Helm and Carnell Tate, who is Questionable. Tony Pollard runs into a Houston run defense at -23.6% DVOA, with his rushing line at 48.5. Houston wins 22-15. That's seven points, exactly the Bookmaker spread and a push on the key number, and the total lands just under 37.5.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">The Opus run passes at zero edge on both side and total. The only tier-eligible pick is Dave Tuley's (VSiN) Titans +7.5, and Steve Makinen's matching near-miss is from the same outlet. Both need +7.5. The current number is +7, and crossing 7 makes it a different bet, so it can't support a play. The registry splits 7 on HOU, including <a href="#exp-hou-ten-action-network">Action Network</a>, <a href="#exp-hou-ten-bettingpros">BettingPros</a>, <a href="#exp-hou-ten-chad-millman">Chad Millman</a>, Pro Football Talk, Ryan Wormeli and <a href="#exp-hou-ten-sharp-or-square">Sharp or Square</a>. Four are on TEN: Dave Tuley, <a href="#exp-hou-ten-even-money">Even Money</a>, <a href="#exp-hou-ten-even-money">Steve Fezzik</a> and Steve Makinen. Action Network also has the lone Under. Spread bets are 68% Houston with 63% of the money, so Tennessee's 37% of money on 32% of bets is a 5-point lean, not a sharp signal. The moneyline is lopsided at 94% Houston. A provisional model has Houston by about 5, but it is unbacktested and moves nothing. Our projection sits on the 7, so it doesn't support the earlier research-only TEN +7 lean. Our 37 is half a point under the 37.5 total, while 77% of bets are on the Over. The 04:00 PT capture expires before the 10:00 PT kickoff, so prices must be recaptured.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Houston's offensive line. Braden Smith is on IR and three more linemen are Questionable, and Houston falls to -0.857 EPA per dropback under pressure. If two or more of them sit, Stroud's edge shrinks toward a field-goal game and Tennessee covers. The other way: if Carnell Tate, Tennessee's target leader (12 targets in Week 4), is inactive, Ward loses his main read. Houston's 8.8% sack rate then produces short fields that push the margin into double digits. A quarterback change on either side voids this read entirely.</p>

<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">This is a slow, wet field-goal game. Deshaun Watson starts with Dillon Gabriel listed Out. Cleveland leans on Quinshon Judkins, whose rushing total is 59.5 and who has cleared that once in four weeks, and Watson throws to Jerry Jeudy, KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. on a MEDIUM secondary matchup. Geno Smith plays without Breece Hall (listed Out), so Garrett Wilson (+143 anytime TD) is New York's main threat, and Braelon Allen has the board's shortest TD price at -119. Neither team runs well (-0.275 and -0.193 EPA per rush), and both run only 57.5 plays a game. The forecast calls for a 78% chance of rain. Cleveland's pass rush, missing Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr., gives Smith just enough time. New York wins by two, and Cleveland covers +2.5 by a half point, a coin flip just below 3.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Treat any lean below as a research-only parlay candidate, not a recommended bet. The lone tier-eligible pick, VSiN's NYJ moneyline at -130, has since moved to -135/-140. The public has 84% of spread tickets on Cleveland. The projected 40 is a half point over 39.5, so there's no total lean either. Recommendation windows close at 04:00 PT, before the 10:00 PT kickoff, so prices need a recapture.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">If Will McDonald IV and Kingsley Enagbare (both Questionable) sit, a rush that pressures only 16.8% of dropbacks gets thinner. <div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>

Pittsburgh wins by three: a push at Bookmaker's -3, a cover at BEO's -2.5, and 43 points against a 43.5 total.</p>

The weather-only Under (-0.5 point from gusts) is research only, not a play. Windows close at 04:00 PT, before kickoff, so prices must be recaptured.</p>

<div class="game-narrative" style="border-left: 4px solid var(--accent); background: rgba(0,210,190,0.07); padding: 12px 16px; border-radius: 8px; margin: 4px 0 16px 0;">
<div style="font-size: 1.08rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 4px;">🎯 Projected final: LAR 29, BUF 26</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; opacity: 0.85; margin-bottom: 8px;">lines imply LAR 29.0 – BUF 25.5 · projected margin LAR by 3 → covers: BUF (LAR -3.5) · total 55 vs 54.5 → Over</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.86rem; margin-bottom: 8px;">📈 <strong>Line movement</strong> (opening line: Action Network open, Sun 10/4 5:00 PM PT → Bookmaker now, 2026-10-11): spread LAR -2.5 → -3.5 · total 53.5 → 54.5 · moneyline BUF +120 → +157 · moneyline LAR -142 → -179</div>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">📖 Game script</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Monday night should be a shootout. Buffalo has the best offense on the field (0.162 EPA per play to the Rams' 0.003), but its pass defense is the worst unit in the game, and the Rams drop back on 63.8% of plays. Matthew Stafford leans on Puka Nacua (receiving line 92.5) and Kyren Williams, the shortest anytime-TD price on the board at -181. Josh Allen answers with his legs near the goal line (7 rushing TDs in four games) and with James Cook III, Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir. Myles Garrett's IR listing on the ESPN injury report should give Allen cleaner pockets, while Ed Oliver being out thins Buffalo's rush. The Rams win 29-26: a three-point margin lands half a point inside the 3.5 spread, so Buffalo covers by the hook in what the simulator treats as a coin flip.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">🧠 Why the card leans this way</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">Treat any lean below as a research-only parlay candidate, not a recommended bet. The Opus run rated it a pass, tier skip, with zero edge on the side and the total. Its only tier-eligible rows come from one outlet, VSiN, and both are different bets (Rams -3 at -120, and a Bills teaser with Over 48.5); another VSiN row backs Buffalo +3. The registry has 7 on BUF, including <a href="#exp-buf-lar-bettingpros">Andrew Erickson</a>, <a href="#exp-buf-lar-bettingpros">BettingPros</a>, <a href="#exp-buf-lar-daniel-jeremiah-bucky-brooks">Daniel Jeremiah & Bucky Brooks</a>, Ryan Wormeli and <a href="#exp-buf-lar-sharp-or-square">Sharp or Square</a>, plus <a href="#exp-buf-lar-even-money">Even Money</a> and <a href="#exp-buf-lar-simon-hunter">Simon Hunter</a>, and 5 on LAR: <a href="#exp-buf-lar-action-network">Action Network</a>, Matt Perrault, Matt Youmans, Pro Football Talk and <a href="#exp-buf-lar-even-money">Steve Fezzik</a>, with <a href="#exp-buf-lar-joe-gibbs">Joe Gibbs</a> also on the Rams. The public is on Buffalo (74% of spread bets, 64% of money). The Rams draw 36% of the money on 26% of the bets, a 10-point gap, short of the 15-point big-money flag. Most side picks were made at 3; the line is now 3.5. Our 55 is half a point over the 54.5 total, inside the noise. These prices lapse Sun 05:21 PT, about 36 hours before kickoff, and must be recaptured.</p>
<div style="font-weight: 700; margin-top: 8px;">⚠️ What breaks it</div>
<p style="margin: 4px 0 6px 0;">DJ Moore (questionable) and Shakir (a setback in the availability digest only) both miss. With Joshua Palmer already out, Allen's passing game narrows to Kincaid and the Rams pull away by a touchdown or more. Or the Rams' 6 interceptions in four games become two more, handing Buffalo short fields and an outright road win.</p>

<summary>🧭 Section 7: What the Experts Say: Consensus & Clashes</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">




**What the experts are saying, counted fairly.** We collect picks from betting podcasts, YouTube shows and betting writers, then count each source **once per game** on the side it picked most. A lopsided count (for example 6–1) means broad agreement; a **clash** means credible sources are split. The table ranks games from the strongest agreement down.

<details class="rollup-box section-3" id="consensus-defs">
<summary>📖 How to read this section</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">

- **Source:** one outlet, podcast host or writer. Outlets that publish several writers (ESPN, VSiN) still count as one vote.
- **For – Against:** sources backing the consensus side vs. the other side. Ties inside one source are dropped.
- **Strength** (the table is ordered by this first): 🌟 Near-unanimous = at least 3× as many sources on one side, or none against · 🔥 Majority = ahead by 2 or more · ⚔️ Clash = ahead by only 1 · ⚖️ Split = dead even.
- **Total lean:** whether more sources picked the Over or the Under.
- **Agreement is not a guarantee.** Heavy consensus on a popular side can already be priced into the line; see the big-money column in Section 6.

[⬆ Back to Our Picks](#recommendations)
</div>
</details>

## 9. Betting Trends & Systems

<div class="rollup-controls">
  <button class="btn-toggle btn-primary" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-9', true)">Expand Section 9</button>
  <button class="btn-toggle" onclick="toggleRollups('secmain-9', false)">Collapse Section 9</button>

<details class="rollup-box section-main secmain-9" id="section-9-box" open>
<summary>📐 Section 9: Betting Trends & Systems</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">



**Betting trends are history, not a forecast.** A record like "11-0 against the spread" can be real and still be luck; use trends to break ties between picks you already like, not as a reason on their own. Below, every trend we captured this week is tied to the game and the side it points to.

<details class="rollup-box section-8" id="under-the-hood" open>
<summary>🔧 Under the hood: how the card was built (ticket list &amp; season build rules)</summary>
<div class="rollup-content">


**Build rules from the season record:**

| # | Rule | Evidence (season, unique legs) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No −120 to −100 connector legs** unless sourcing tier 1–2 (Section 4). Take −121 or longer, or plus money. | 31-45-1, 41% vs 53% needed, −23% (n=76), bad both weeks |
| 2 | **Underdog spreads are allowed when the matchup and price case are stated.** Do not use points merely to make a parlay leg feel safer. | Week 1 spread dogs were 10-20, −44%; that is a review signal, not a prohibition. |
| 3 | **Lean on tackles+assists and passing TDs.** Keep sacks and receiving yards to a minimum. | T+A 9-4 +22%, pass TD 8-3 +14%; rec yds −27%, receptions −18%, sacks 2-3 |
| 4 | **Each starting QB is one shared risk** across every leg on his offense. Count those legs as one exposure. | MNF Dart injury: Giants legs 4-15 |
| 5 | **ML chalk ≤ −290 is not a free anchor.** Flag it; one per ticket at most. | 6-4 vs ~78% implied; TB −410, BAL −379, LAC −292 all lost |
| 6 | **Receptions are tight to the line.** Only for proven target share on the expected winner. Yardage is bimodal, so don't pay −110 to −120 for a median line. | 9 of 12 rec losses were within 1.5 catches |
| 7 | Bookmaker vs BetOnline: **no edge either way** (50% vs 49% after the 9/22 book correction). Choose the book by rule and price, not habit. | — |
